scheduling.skillGoal: Review document structure and propose prioritized cuts, reorganization, condensation, and preservation recommendations to improve clarity and flow before copy editing
scheduling.intentSignature: Structural-edit a document for high-value density and propose recommendations
intentSignatures: Structural-edit a document for high-value density and propose recommendations
Run a structural review or editorial review of structure
Propose cuts, merges, moves, and condensations on a document
Optimize a document's structure before copy editing
triggerPatterns: user requests structural review or editorial review of structure
user asks to optimize document structure before copy editing

ioContract.inputsRaw: content (required) — Document to review (markdown, plain text, or structured content). style_guide (optional) — overrides all generic principles except CONTENT IS SACROSANCT. purpose (optional). target_audience (optional). reader_type (optional, default `humans`). length_target (optional, e.g. '30% shorter').
ioContract.outputsRaw: Markdown block: ## Document Summary (Purpose, Audience, Reader type, Structure model, Current length); ## Recommendations (numbered entries with [CUT/MERGE/MOVE/CONDENSE/QUESTION/PRESERVE] - section name, Rationale, Impact ~X words, optional Comprehension note); ## Summary (Total recommendations, Estimated reduction, Meets length target, Comprehension trade-offs). Or 'No substantive changes recommended -- document structure is sound'.

preconditions: reader_type is `humans` or `llm` (or omitted, defaulting to `humans`)
document headings, sections, and lists are detectable for structural mapping

structural.sceneGoal: Validate inputs (length, reader_type), identify document type and structure, and note current word and section counts
Resolve or infer purpose and target_audience, state the document's existence in one sentence, and select the appropriate structure model
Map document structure with section word counts and evaluate against the selected model's primary rules to find cuts, merges, moves, redundancies, scope violations, and burying
Assess reader's journey, premature detail, missing scaffolding, anti-patterns, and human pacing to surface flow issues
Compile findings into prioritized recommendations with category, rationale, and impact; flag comprehension trade-offs for human readers
Output the document summary, prioritized recommendations, and estimated reduction; otherwise output 'No substantive changes recommended'

logical.description: If content is empty or fewer than 3 words, HALT with the documented error
If reader_type is provided and is not `humans` or `llm`, HALT with the documented error
Identify document type and structure (headings, sections, lists, etc.) and note current word count and section count
Use provided purpose and target_audience or infer them from content; identify the core question the document answers
State in one sentence: 'This document exists to help [audience] accomplish [goal]'

Select the most appropriate structure model (Tutorial/Guide, Reference/Database, Explanation, Prompt/Task Definition, Strategic/Context) and apply Human-Reader or LLM-Reader principles per reader_type
If style_guide was provided, consult it now and treat its requirements as overriding default principles for this analysis
Map the document structure with each major section's word count and evaluate against the selected model's primary rules (e.g., 'Does recommendation come first?' for Pyramid)
For each section, decide whether to cut, merge, move, or split; identify true redundancies, scope violations, and buried critical information; for humans, evaluate comprehension aids individually
Assess reader's journey, premature detail, missing scaffolding, anti-patterns (FAQs that should be inline, appendices to cut, body-repeating overviews), and pacing for humans
Compile findings into prioritized recommendations and categorize each as CUT, MERGE, MOVE, CONDENSE, QUESTION, or PRESERVE
For each recommendation, write a one-sentence rationale and estimate impact in words (saved or, for PRESERVE, cost)
If length_target was provided, assess whether recommendations meet it; if reader_type='humans' and recommendations would cut comprehension aids, flag with a comprehension warning

Output Document Summary, prioritized Recommendations list, and Summary (totals, estimated reduction, length target met, comprehension trade-offs) per the documented markdown format; otherwise emit 'No substantive changes recommended -- document structure is sound'
